description: Former New York Times labor reporter Steve Greenhouse talks with Recode's Kara Swisher about his most recent book, Beaten Down, Worked Up: The Past, Present, and Future of American Labor. Greenhouse explains why worker power and compensation are at their lowest levels since World War II and how a series of cultural changes — including globalization, the internet, and the gig economy — have affected and endangered the working class. classificationReason: Includes a substantial discussion of artificial intelligence, UBI, worker power, and technology-driven labor changes, though robotics is not central.
qualityReason: Named expert interview with developed analysis of labor, technology, and AI policy.
